pr_title: Unnamed fields states (substates) support in derive(States)
pr_body:
# Objective
- Fixes #8187 
## Solution
TODO
This requires that all unnamed fields implement States too, obviously.
~~This does not work yet, since we have to convert Vec's IntoIter type into array's IntoIter type, which isn't possible, since we have to specify the length at runtime. Unfortunately we can't get the variants length at compile time.~~ Now works.

## Changelog
- Added support for enum fields states in #[derive(States)]

## Migration Guide
The Self::Iter type of "fieldful" enums that derive the States macro is `std::vec::IntoIter` rather than `std::array::IntoIter`, which remains to be the Iter type of fieldless enums. This is because child variations have to be collected at runtime. This does not change anything in the [State](https://docs.rs/bevy/latest/bevy/ecs/prelude/trait.States.html) trait though, so users are less likely to be affected.

However, this might affect some edge cases, so I think I will include this just so that everyone know this detail..

issue_context.title: Add support for enum fields in the #[derive(States)
issue_context.body:
## What problem does this solve or what need does it fill?
For me, I'm developing a visual novel engine. I wrote a state for managing the navigation of the app. Since this engine focuses on extensibility, there needs a way for users to add their own state to work inside my state. In Rust, that's possible with type arguments and fields (`enum Foobar(T){ Foo, Bar(T), }`)

That's also how it was done in [Inox2d](https://docs.rs/inox2d/latest/inox2d/nodes/node_data/enum.InoxData.html). 

However, in the implementation of the States derive macro, [enum fields are not supported](       https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/blob/4f16d6e0dc14c12ab29b72880d5d3d22003eed72/crates/bevy_ecs/macros/src/states.rs#LL12C15-L12C15).

## What solution would you like?
As described in issue title.

## What alternative(s) have you considered?
We can implement `States` manually, but won't that be tedious?

Or we can "flatten" the enums. So from:
```rs
pub enum Foo {
   Fieldless
   Bar(Bar)
}
pub enum Bar {
   Alice,
   Bob
}
```
to:
```rs
pub enum Foo {
 Fieldless,
 BarAlice,
 BarBob
}
```

But for adding states that we can't control (e.g. user-defined states), that won't be possible.

## Additional context
N/A
comments: This is possible in bevy 0.13, so this can be closed.
And this pattern will be much better supported in general with the upcoming computed and sub states support in 0.14.

review_comments: It would be nice to be able to split apart these error cases, but I won't block on it.

But since you support it, great!
